facts.claim: A neuroprosthesis achieved 90.2% accuracy using a 125,000-word vocabulary after 1.4 additional hours of system training on the second day.
facts.quote: On the second day, after 1. 4 additional hours of system training, the neuroprosthesis achieved 90. 2% accuracy using a 125,000-word vocabulary.

facts.claim: A person with ALS and severe dysarthria used a speech neuroprosthesis to communicate in self-paced conversations at a rate of approximately 32 words per minute for more than 248 cumulative hours.
facts.quote: the participant used it to communicate in self-paced conversations at a rate of approximately 32 words per minute for more than 248 cumulative hours.

facts.claim: A participant's attempted speech was decoded at 62 words per minute, which is 3.4 times as fast as the previous record.
facts.quote: Our participant's attempted speech was decoded at 62 words per minute, which is 3. 4 times as fast as the previous record

facts.claim: A multimodal speech-neuroprosthetic approach demonstrated accurate and rapid large-vocabulary decoding with a median rate of 78 words per minute and median word error rate of 25%.
facts.quote: For text, we demonstrate accurate and rapid large-vocabulary decoding with a median rate of 78 words per minute and median word error rate of 25%.

facts.claim: A person with anarthria and spastic quadriparesis caused by a brain-stem stroke had sentences decoded from cortical activity at a median rate of 15.2 words per minute with a median word error rate of 25.6%.
facts.quote: We decoded sentences from the participant's cortical activity in real time at a median rate of 15. 2 words per minute, with a median word error rate of 25. 6%.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: A high-performance intracortical BCI was tested by three clinical trial participants with paralysis and exceeded previous iBCIs by a factor of 1.4-4.2 in typing rate.
facts.quote: For all three participants, performance exceeded previous iBCIs (Bacher et al. , 2015; Jarosiewicz et al. , 2015) as measured by typing rate (by a factor of 1. 4-4. 2)

research.angle: Brain-computer interfaces can decode attempted speech into text or audio at various speeds, ranging from 15.2 to 78 words per minute depending on the specific system and participant.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that speech neuroprostheses can decode cortical activity into words and sentences for people with paralysis, with some systems reaching high accuracy and conversational speeds.
research.caveat: The performance of these systems varies significantly across different studies, with word rates ranging from 15.2 to 78 words per minute.
